sources.entry: MacDirStat - Open-source disk space analyzer that shows what's taking up space as an interactive treemap, inspired by WinDirStat. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/phalladar/MacDirStat) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: MacDirStat is a free, open-source native macOS disk space analyzer that scans a drive or folder and shows file sizes as a color-coded treemap, inspired by WinDirStat.
summary.what_it_does: It scans a chosen drive, mounted volume, or custom folder and draws each file as a rectangle sized by disk usage, nested within its folders using a squarified treemap layout. Files are colored by category (documents, images, video, audio, code, archives, applications, system, caches, other) based on file extension. A folder tree sidebar lists folders largest first, and an inspector shows size, allocated size, file and folder counts, last-modified date, and a per-type breakdown. Users can double-click to drill into folders, zoom and pan, switch between File Size and Allocated Size, and reveal files in Finder or copy paths. The app is read-only and never deletes or moves files itself; it has no networking code, and it measures iCloud/OneDrive placeholders without downloading them, marking cloud-only folders as incomplete.
use_cases: find what is taking up space on a Mac
clean up a full startup disk
measure size of a specific folder before deleting
review large files and their locations
how_to_run: Download MacDirStat.zip from the releases page and unzip it
Drag MacDirStat.app into the Applications folder
Open MacDirStat and click Open when macOS asks to confirm
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd MacDirStat, swift build -c release
Run from source with: swift run MacDirStat
To install a built app: ./scripts/build-app.sh, then cp -R .build/MacDirStat.app /Applications/
notable: Interactive squarified treemap with color-coded file categories and drill-down navigation
Cloud-aware scanning that measures File Provider placeholders without downloading contents
No networking code, no analytics, no update checks; read-only
Zero external dependencies, native SwiftUI app
Hard-linked files counted once; parallel scanning with live progress
caveats: Requires macOS 15 Sequoia or later; does not run on macOS 14 or earlier
Full Disk Access is optional but needed to include protected folders like Mail and Messages; totals can be lower without it
Scan totals can differ from macOS Storage settings; APFS snapshots and cloud-only folders are not fully counted
keywords: what is taking up space mac
